goal: Let a request carrying a valid x-ingest-token header reach a named, explicit list of routes (GET /api/status, ACARS read/write routes, GET /api/ground-sessions/current) without a session cookie, while every other /api route stays cookie-only exactly as today. This widens the scope of the existing INGEST_TOKEN — no new secret, no login flow, no prefix/wildcard bypass.
frozen_decisions: Chosen: "Extend ingest-token scope" — Add a token-authorized path for GET /api/status, the ACARS read/write routes, and ground-session reads — same shared secret the agent already uses, no cookie, no login UI. Keeps the sidecar-owns-the-token boundary they already built. Requires a server-side change here (auth middleware) scoped carefully so the token can't do everything a session can.

Chosen: "Widen the existing INGEST_TOKEN" — Simplest: one shared secret, already deployed to the agent and the sidecar's config.json. New server-side auth path checks the same token for GET /api/status, the ACARS read/write routes, and ground-session reads. A leak exposes telemetry ingest plus ACARS/loadsheet/WX access, but nothing session-only (flight history browsing, account settings, etc.).
The user explicitly did not choose a second/separate datalink token, and did not choose a client-side login flow. Both alternatives are out of scope for this run.
keep the enumeration explicit, matching how /api/ingest/* is already special-cased in requireSameOrigin today, not a prefix/wildcard match
ground-session writes (POST /ground-sessions, DELETE /ground-sessions/current) are deliberately left off this list unless Designer finds a concrete need
No DevOps phase — no build/packaging/deploy/CI/secrets change
sequencing_rationale: This changes the server's auth contract, not a route body, so Design must freeze the mechanism (new scoped middleware vs. a global requireAuth change), the finalized route list, the requireSameOrigin interaction, and the error contract before any code moves — per project convention, a contract change always gets a Design phase.

Implementation is one seam: the new middleware in src/auth/middleware.ts and its mount points in src/server.ts are edited together by one backend_sr task, since splitting the middleware definition from its wiring would just be two cold reads of the same design slice for no parallelism (both files are read/write by the same task, so there is nothing to parallelize).

Review is its own phase, gated after implementation, because the acceptance criterion this run cares most about — routes NOT on the list must still reject a token-only request with 401 — is a security regression check that has to run against a live scratch server, not just a diff read.
No DevOps phase: intake explicitly skips it, this run has no build/packaging/deploy/secrets surface.

tasks.title: Design requireAuthOrIngestToken: mechanism, route list, requireSameOrigin interaction, error contract
tasks.goal: Freeze the auth-contract change described in the intake (.claude/runs/2026-09-16-ingest-token-acars-scope/intake.md — read it in full first, it is the source of truth for this task and is ~110 lines). Design a new middleware (name it requireAuthOrIngestToken or equivalent) that accepts EITHER a valid session (req.session.user, same check as the existing requireAuth in src/auth/middleware.ts lines 7-18) OR a valid x-ingest-token header (same SHA-256/timingSafeEqual comparison src/ingest.ts already does at lines 116-120 and 167-178, against config.ingest.token from src/config.ts — do not write a second comparison implementation). It must be mounted ONLY on the specific routes in the finalized list below — never as a replacement for the blanket `app.use('/api', requireAuth)` at src/server.ts line 81, which every other route must keep relying on unchanged. Work out and document the concrete mounting mechanism given that requireAuth already runs globally before every router in src/server.ts (lines 81, 134, 140, 146, 153, 158, 165, 171) — e.g. whether the scoped middleware runs before the blanket requireAuth and marks the request as authenticated so requireAuth becomes a no-op for it, or whether GET /api/status and the routers in src/routes/acars.ts and src/routes/groundSessions.ts move to their own per-router mount ahead of the blanket requireAuth line with the new middleware applied per-route inside them. Whichever shape is chosen, the design must show, route by route, that a request to anything NOT on the list still hits the unchanged requireAuth and gets 401 on a token-only request — this is the property Review will verify against a live server, so state precisely which code path produces that 401 for an off-list route. Finalize the route list against the candidates in the intake (GET /api/status; GET /api/acars/canned-messages; GET and POST /api/flights/:id/acars-messages; POST /api/flights/:id/acars-messages/wx; GET and POST /api/planned-legs/:legId/acars-messages; POST /api/planned-legs/:legId/acars-messages/wx; POST /api/planned-legs/:legId/acars-messages/loadsheet; GET /api/ground-sessions/current) — drop any route you cannot justify against a concrete sidecar need already stated in the intake, do not add any. Specify the requireSameOrigin interaction: src/auth/middleware.ts lines 25-59, specifically the existing /api/ingest/* exemption at lines 39-42 — the newly-scoped routes need the same treatment (no Origin required) when hit with a token and no cookie, without loosening the CSRF check for the same route hit with a cookie and an Origin header. Specify the error contract: exact status codes and JSON body shapes for (a) no token and no cookie on a scoped route, (b) wrong token and no cookie on a scoped route, (c) valid token but the route is not on the scoped list. Match the existing shape conventions (src/auth/middleware.ts line 17 `{ error: 'Authentication required' }`, src/ingest.ts line 176 `{ error: 'Invalid or missing ingest token' }`) rather than inventing a new envelope, and state whether scoped-route failures reuse one of those bodies verbatim or need a distinct one — the sidecar needs to tell 'not reachable' from 'wrong token' from 'not authorized for this route' per the intake. Include a worked table of every route on the final list against its middleware chain (which functions run, in what order) so the implementer does not have to re-derive it.
acceptance_criteria: design.md states the exact middleware mounting mechanism (function names, file, line-level insertion point) for src/auth/middleware.ts and src/server.ts, with a route-by-route table showing which middleware chain each of the finalized routes and one off-list example route (e.g. GET /api/flights) run through

design.md's finalized route list is a subset of the intake's candidate list, each entry justified against a concrete sidecar need already stated in the intake — no route added beyond the candidates, any dropped route says why

design.md specifies the requireSameOrigin change (or explicit non-change) needed so a token-bearing, cookie-less, Origin-less request to a scoped route is not rejected by the CSRF check, referencing src/auth/middleware.ts lines 39-42 as the existing precedent

design.md specifies the exact status code and JSON body for each of: no-credential request to a scoped route, wrong-token request to a scoped route, valid-token request to an off-list route, matching or explicitly extending the existing error-body conventions in src/auth/middleware.ts:17 and src/ingest.ts:176

design.md explicitly confirms the token comparison reuses the sha256/timingSafeEqual helper pattern from src/ingest.ts (lines 116-120, 167-178) rather than a new implementation, and names where the shared comparison lives after this change (e.g. extracted into src/auth/middleware.ts or a shared module) so the implementer does not have two copies
